definition: a different option or choice
example: Public transport is a practical alternative to driving in busy cities.

definition: a fact or condition connected with an event or situation
example: Under normal circumstances, the flight would have taken three hours.

definition: to express an opinion about something
example: Experts have commented on the potential risks of artificial intelligence.

definition: to give someone something to make up for a loss, damage, or harm
example: The airline compensated passengers for the delayed flight.

definition: a part of a larger whole, especially a machine or system
example: Regular exercise is an essential component of a healthy lifestyle.

definition: permission for something to happen
example: Doctors must obtain a patient's consent before starting treatment.

definition: notably large in size, amount, or extent
example: The new policy required a considerable amount of government funding.

definition: occurring continuously; not changing
example: Rapid technological change puts constant pressure on workers to learn new skills.

definition: to limit or restrict someone's freedom to act
example: Limited funding constrains what schools can offer students.

definition: to give something, especially money, effort, or ideas, to help achieve a result
example: Everyone in the office contributed ideas for the new project.

definition: to come together, or bring people together, for a formal meeting
example: World leaders convened to discuss strategies for tackling climate change.

definition: to organize different people or things so they work together effectively
example: The event required several departments to coordinate their efforts.

definition: central and most important
example: Reading and writing are core skills taught in primary school.

definition: relating to a large company or business
example: Many corporate offices now allow employees to work remotely.

definition: to match or be consistent with something
example: The rise in house prices does not correspond with an increase in wages.

definition: standards used as a basis for judging or deciding something
example: Universities use a range of criteria to select students.

definition: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from available evidence
example: From the data, researchers deduced that diet has a strong effect on health.

definition: to clearly show that something is true, usually with evidence
example: The study demonstrates a clear link between exercise and happiness.

definition: to record something in written, photographic, or other permanent form
example: Journalists documented the effects of the flood on local communities.

definition: to have a controlling influence over something
example: A few large companies dominate the global smartphone market.

definition: special importance or attention given to something
example: Modern education places greater emphasis on critical thinking than memorization.

definition: to make certain that something happens or is the case
example: Governments must ensure that all children have access to education.

definition: to deliberately leave someone or something out
example: The report excludes data from before 2010.

definition: a basic structure underlying a system, plan, or concept
example: The new law provides a legal framework for protecting consumer rights.

definition: to provide money for a particular purpose
example: The project is funded by a combination of government grants and private donations.

definition: to explain or make something clear, often using examples or images
example: The graph illustrates the sharp rise in unemployment during the recession.

definition: to come to live permanently in a foreign country
example: Thousands of skilled workers immigrate to the country each year.

definition: to suggest something indirectly, without stating it outright
example: The report implies that current policies are not working effectively.

definition: existing or occurring at the beginning
example: The initial results of the trial were promising.

definition: an example or single occurrence of something
example: There have been several instances of data theft at large companies.

definition: to communicate with or react to one another
example: Social media has changed the way young people interact with one another.

definition: to show or prove that something is reasonable or right
example: It can be difficult to justify the high cost of university tuition.

definition: a level, thickness, or covering of material lying over or under another
example: There is an extra layer of bureaucracy that slows down the approval process.

definition: a connection or relationship between two things
example: Studies have found a clear link between diet and mental health.

definition: to find the exact position of something, or to situate something in a particular place
example: The company decided to locate its new factory near the coast.

definition: to make the best or most effective use of something
example: Companies are always looking for ways to maximise profit while cutting costs.

definition: small or relatively unimportant
example: The changes to the timetable were minor and did not affect most students.

definition: to cancel out or make something ineffective
example: The benefits of exercise can be negated by an unhealthy diet.

definition: the result or effect of an action or event
example: The outcome of the negotiations will affect thousands of workers.

definition: a person or organization that works jointly with another
example: The charity works closely with corporate partners to fund local projects.

definition: a theory or set of beliefs that guides someone's behavior or approach
example: The school's philosophy emphasizes creativity over rote memorization.

definition: relating to the body, as opposed to the mind
example: Regular physical activity is essential for both children and adults.

definition: a part or share of a whole, especially in relation to its size
example: A large proportion of the population now works from home at least part-time.

definition: to make information available to the public, especially in print
example: The findings were published in an international journal.

definition: to respond to something that happens
example: Markets reacted quickly to the announcement of new trade tariffs.

definition: to record something officially, or to enrol formally for something
example: All new businesses must register with the local authority.

definition: to depend on someone or something
example: Many rural communities rely heavily on agriculture for income.

definition: to take something away or eliminate it
example: The new regulations aim to remove unnecessary red tape for small businesses.

definition: a formal plan or system, often organized by a government or institution
example: The government launched a scheme to help first-time home buyers.

definition: a particular order in which related events or actions happen
example: Understanding the sequence of events helped investigators solve the case.

definition: a change in position, attitude, or emphasis
example: There has been a significant shift toward online shopping in recent years.

definition: to state something clearly and exactly
example: The contract specifies the exact working hours and responsibilities.

definition: enough for a particular purpose
example: Many families do not have sufficient income to cover basic living costs.

definition: a piece of work to be done, especially one done regularly or as part of a job
example: Managers should delegate routine tasks to free up time for planning.

definition: relating to a particular practical skill or specialized field of knowledge
example: The job requires strong technical skills in data analysis.

definition: a particular way of doing something, especially one requiring skill
example: Teachers are using new techniques to make lessons more engaging.

definition: the practical application of scientific knowledge, especially in machinery and equipment
example: New technology has made remote work far more efficient.

definition: legally or logically acceptable; sound
example: Passengers must show a valid ticket before boarding the train.

definition: the amount or quantity of something
example: The volume of online shopping has increased dramatically in the past decade.
